title: Dated end-of-support notices for platforms, crypto, parsers and services

prose.text: Each notice below is what it says on its announcement date. The 3DES notices name their scope: IKE Phase 2 for IPSec, and SSL.

prose.label: ZscalerOS 10 virtual machines.
prose.text: {{zscaleros-10}} {{zscaleros-10-aws}} {{zscaleros-10-esxi}} Whether AWS and ESXi customers had to act is in dispute {{divergence:zscaleros-10-action-required}}. The ZscalerOS 24 target is covered in [[cloud-connector.upgrades.os-images]].

prose.label: Hypervisor and Linux platforms.
prose.text: {{esxi-55}} The ESXi minimum differs from other pages {{divergence:esxi-minimum-version}}. {{el7}}

prose.label: Authentication.
prose.text: {{sms-otp}} Whether the disablement has happened is open {{gap:sms-otp-status}}.

zscaleros-10.statement: The Azure notice dated March 11, 2022 says Azure Virtual Machine deployments with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier are no longer supported for ZIA Virtual Service Edges, VZENs and NSS as of June 24, 2022, and that the migration target is ZscalerOS version 24 or higher; it says no action is required for customers with VMs on AWS or ESXi.

quotes: Azure Virtual Machine deployments with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier are no longer supported for ZIA Virtual Service Edges, VZENs, and NSS as of June 24, 2022
migrate to ZscalerOS version 24 or higher by June 24, 2022
No action is required for customers with virtual machines (VMs) on AWS or ESXi; these VMs are being upgraded remotely and automatically.
Announcement date: March 11, 2022

zscaleros-10-aws.statement: The AWS notice dated May 4, 2022 says Amazon Web Services Virtual Machine deployments with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier are no longer supported for NSS as of June 24, 2022.

quotes: Amazon Web Services Virtual Machine deployments with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier are no longer supported for NSS as of June 24, 2022.
Announcement date: May 4, 2022

zscaleros-10-esxi.statement: The ESXi notice dated May 4, 2022 says VMware ESXi Virtual Machine deployments with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier are no longer supported for Index Tool, NSS, ZAB, ZIA Virtual Service Edge, VZEN and Zscaler Incident Receiver as of June 24, 2022.

quotes: are no longer supported for Index Tool, NSS, ZAB, ZIA Virtual Service Edge, VZEN, and Zscaler Incident Receiver as of June 24, 2022
Announcement date: May 4, 2022

esxi-55.statement: The notice dated January 26, 2024 says Zscaler will no longer support ESXi version 5.5 after December 24, 2024, and that customers currently using ESXi version 5.5 will need ESXi version 7.0 Update 2 or later after this date.

quotes: Zscaler will no longer support ESXi version 5.5 after December 24, 2024.
Customers currently using ESXi version 5.5 will need to use ESXi version 7.0 Update 2 or later after this date.
Announcement date: January 26, 2024

el7.statement: The notice (revised December 9, 2024) says Zscaler will no longer support App Connectors and Private Service Edges on CentOS 7.x, RHEL 7.x and Oracle Linux 7.x after March 31, 2025, and customers will need to migrate to RHEL 9 or later and the EL9 ZPA repository.

quotes: no longer support App Connectors and Private Service Edges running on CentOS 7.x, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.x (RHEL 7.x), and Oracle Linux 7.x after March 31, 2025
will need to migrate to Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 or later and the EL9 ZPA repository after this date
Announcement date: February 9, 2024
Revised date: December 9, 2024

spidermonkey.statement: The notice dated July 21, 2023 says that on January 31, 2024 Zscaler will no longer support the SpiderMonkey-based PAC parsers and all customers will be moved to the V8 PAC parser.

quotes: On January 31, 2024, Zscaler will no longer support the SpiderMonkey-based PAC parsers.
All customers will be moved to the V8 PAC parser.
Announcement date: July 21, 2023

3des-ipsec.statement: The notice dated August 25, 2017 says Zscaler no longer supports 3DES for IPSec encryption (IKE Phase 2 only), recommends null encryption for IPSec tunnels to the Zscaler service, and says to use AES encryption if IPSec encryption is required for regulatory or compliance reasons and the customer has the appropriate entitlement.

quotes: Zscaler no longer supports 3DES for IPSec encryption (IKE Phase 2 only)
Zscaler recommends that you use null encryption for your IPSec tunnels to the Zscaler service.
If you must encrypt traffic using IPSec (for regulatory or compliance reasons), and you have the appropriate entitlement, use AES encryption.
Announcement date: August 25, 2017

3des-ssl.statement: The notice dated September 13, 2017 says Zscaler will end support of 3DES for SSL after the 5.6 release, clients should change to AES256-GCM-SHA384, AES128-GCM-SHA256, AES256-SHA or AES128-SHA by October 31, 2018, and clients still using 3DES will be unable to connect to websites.

quotes: Zscaler will end support of 3DES for SSL after the 5.6 release.
AES256-GCM-SHA384, AES128-GCM-SHA256, AES256-SHA, or AES128-SHA by October 31, 2018
clients using 3DES will be unable to connect to websites when 3DES support is ended
Announcement date: September 13, 2017

flash-cookies.statement: The notice dated August 14, 2017 says Zscaler discontinued its support for Adobe Flash cookies in the 5.5 release; if no authentication mechanism is configured before support ends, the mechanism already configured on the ZIA Admin Portal is used to authenticate users. The notice describes cookies downloaded from admin.<Zscaler Cloud Name>/download/cookies as Flash cookie use.

quotes: Zscaler discontinued its support for Adobe Flash cookies in the 5.5 release.
If you do not configure an authentication mechanism before Zscaler ends its support for Adobe Flash cookies
You are using Adobe Flash cookies if you downloaded cookies from https://admin.<Zscaler Cloud Name>/download/cookies
the Zscaler service will use the authentication mechanism that is already configured on the ZIA Admin Portal to authenticate users
Announcement date: August 14, 2017

sms-otp.statement: The notice dated May 20, 2026 gives May 22, 2026 as the date SMS MFA enrollment is no longer available for new tenants created after the announcement date, and says SMS-based OTP for hosted users and hosted admins of Authentication Service is disabled for sign-in as of August 07, 2026.

quotes: As of August 07, 2026, Authentication Service will no longer support SMS-based one-time passcodes (OTP) for multi-factor authentication (MFA) for hosted users and hosted admins.
SMS MFA enrollment will no longer be available for new tenants created post the announcement date.
SMS MFA will be disabled for sign-in.
Announcement date: May 20, 2026

cc-repo-cert.statement: The notice dated October 8, 2026 says the TLS certificate for the Cloud Connector software update repository expires on March 18, 2027, and says customers must update their virtual machines or use the latest marketplace images, which Zscaler recommends completing by December 31, 2026; for existing Cloud Connector deployments it says no action is required because Zscaler is deploying an automatic update to the CA trust bundle, while new deployments after March 18, 2027 require the updated marketplace image. Cloud Connector or Branch Connector VMs below version 1.146 lack the DigiCert G2 certificate chain; the March 2026 patch is included in Cloud Connector 1.146.5 or higher and Branch Connector 1.146.0 or higher.

quotes: The TLS certificate for the Zscaler Cloud Connector software update repository will expire on March 18, 2027.
customers must update their virtual machines or use the latest marketplace images
Zscaler recommends that all customers complete these updates by December 31, 2026
Existing Cloud Connector Deployments: No action is required. Zscaler is deploying an automatic update to patch the CA trust bundle. No restart is required.
New Cloud Connector Deployments: The updated marketplace image is required when deploying new Cloud Connectors after March 18, 2027.
running Cloud Connector or Branch Connector virtual machines with versions lower than 1.146
Zscaler published an automatic software patch in March 2026 that recognizes the new DigiCert G2 certificate chain. It is included in the following software versions:
Cloud Connector: Version 1.146.5 or higher
Branch Connector: Version 1.146.0 or higher
Announcement date: October 8, 2026

cc-repo-cert-impact.statement: The same notice says that, if you do not take action before March 18, 2027, existing Cloud Connectors lose the ability to receive future software updates if the automatic fix is not applied, new deployments from older marketplace images cannot connect to the update repository and come online, and Autoscaling Groups or custom templates using old launch templates, warm pool or instance templates spin up instances that cannot connect, resulting in scale out failures.

quotes: If you do not take action before March 18, 2027:
If the automatic fix is not applied, existing Cloud Connectors lose the ability to receive future software updates
Deployments using older marketplace images after March 18, 2027 are unable to connect to the update repository and come online.

ASGs using old launch templates, warm pool (Amazon Web Services (AWS)), or instance templates (Microsoft Azure/Google Cloud Platform (GCP)) spin up new instances that cannot connect to the update repository, resulting in scale out failures.

certificate-downloads.statement: The notice dated July 11, 2023 says that as of September 1, 2023 the certificate download function is removed; Client Connector 2.1 and earlier downloaded the SSL inspection certificate from a CDN, and devices still on 2.1 or earlier continue to function but will not download the certificate if it is not trusted.

quotes: Versions of Zscaler Client Connector 2.1 and earlier downloaded the configured SSL inspection certificate from a cloud-based content delivery network (CDN).
Devices still running version 2.1 or earlier will continue to function
as of September 1, 2023, the certificate download function will be removed
if the SSL certificate is not trusted by the device, it will not be downloaded
Announcement date: July 11, 2023

esxi-minimum-version.summary: The ESXi 5.5 notice says customers will need ESXi 7.0 Update 2 or later after December 24, 2024, while the Index Tool VMware page and the Virtual Service Edge platform table give VMware ESX/ESXi 6.0 or later as the hypervisor requirement.

positions.says: Customers currently using ESXi 5.5 will need ESXi 7.0 Update 2 or later after December 24, 2024.

quotes: Customers currently using ESXi version 5.5 will need to use ESXi version 7.0 Update 2 or later after this date.

positions.says: The Index Tool VMware deployment requires VMware ESX/ESXi version 6.0 or later.

evidence.after: If your index templates include less than 300 million records, Zscaler recommends
quotes: Hypervisor: VMware ESX/ESXi version 6.0 or later.

positions.says: Virtual Service Edge hypervisor support is VMware ESXi 6.0 and later.

quotes: | Hypervisor Support | VMware ESXi 6.0 and later | Microsoft Azure | AWS EC2 | Microsoft Hyper-V | GCP |

esxi-minimum-version.impact: The notice names no product, so whether the 7.0 Update 2 floor applies to Index Tool or Virtual Service Edge, and whether those pages' 6.0 minimum is stale, is not stated.

zscaleros-10-action-required.summary: The Azure ZscalerOS 10 notice says no action is required for customers with VMs on AWS or ESXi because they are upgraded automatically, while the AWS and ESXi notices tell customers running ZscalerOS 10 and earlier on those platforms to migrate to ZscalerOS 24 or higher by June 24, 2022.

positions.says: No action is required for customers with VMs on AWS or ESXi; those VMs are upgraded remotely and automatically (notice dated March 11, 2022).

quotes: No action is required for customers with virtual machines (VMs) on AWS or ESXi; these VMs are being upgraded remotely and automatically.

positions.says: Customers running an AWS VM deployment with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier must migrate to ZscalerOS 24 or higher by June 24, 2022 (notice dated May 4, 2022).

quotes: If your organization is running an Amazon Web Services Virtual Machine deployment with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier, migrate to ZscalerOS version 24 or higher by June 24, 2022, to ensure service continuity.

positions.says: Customers running an ESXi VM deployment with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier must migrate to ZscalerOS 24 or higher by June 24, 2022 (notice dated May 4, 2022).

quotes: If your organization is running an ESXi Virtual Machine deployment with ZscalerOS version 10 and earlier, migrate to ZscalerOS version 24 or higher by June 24, 2022, to ensure service continuity.

zscaleros-10-action-required.impact: An AWS or ESXi customer reading only the Azure notice would take no action, while the later AWS and ESXi notices ask for a migration; the pages do not say whether the later notices replace the Azure notice's statement.

sms-otp-status.title: Whether SMS OTP sign-in has been disabled
sms-otp-status.detail: The notice states the state as of its dates (enrollment closed to new tenants as of May 22, 2026, sign-in disabled as of August 07, 2026); the capture does not say whether the disablement has happened. Whether SMS is a factor in the Authentication Service today is also tracked in zidentity.authentication-methods and zidentity.overview, which this notice bears on.

cc-repo-cert-outcome.title: Outcome of the Cloud Connector repository certificate expiry
cc-repo-cert-outcome.detail: The notice is dated October 8, 2026 with the March 18, 2027 expiry and the December 31, 2026 recommended date still ahead of the capture; no outcome is stated. The notice says versions below 1.146 are impacted and the patch is in Cloud Connector 1.146.5 or higher, but does not say whether Cloud Connector 1.146.0 to 1.146.4 have the DigiCert G2 chain. It also says both that customers must update and that no action is required for existing deployments, without saying who must act. The repository-certificate subject's expiry-date question (old-image-not-listed in cloud-connector.upgrades.repo-certificate) is answered by the March 18, 2027 date here.
